![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039248/assets/a43a1658a16151c0306702959c50e8d0288077983ad50a084b39703e206469c0.png)

Consider the vector $\mathbf{v}$ shown above. Find the vector $A\mathbf{v}$ given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Consider the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors. Computing the images of $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ under $A,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =Ai=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=j \\ {j}^{′} & =Aj=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-i\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039248/assets/414cb72ff004fe4c5898a0e2c7b60b4b3651473e776388fad21efd8fc9ae6165.png)

So, the matrix represents a rotation of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ radians counterclockwise about the origin.

Therefore, in order to find $A\mathbf{v},$ we need to rotate $\mathbf{v}$ counterclockwise by an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ radians, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039248/assets/b24d8d460b7833a49f2bd7183f0f4b5d22d94a7d3b1d3bb9eb51beff9eeb7ef6.png)

feedback.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-1,-2),(-1,2),(1,1).$  Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the **clockwise** rotation ${R}_{-\pi }$ by an angle of $\pi $ radians about the origin?

- $(1,2)$
- $(1,-2)$
- $(-1,-1)$
feedback.worked_solution:
The clockwise rotation ${R}_{-\pi }$ by an angle of $\pi $ radians is the same as counterclockwise rotation by the same angle. It's given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{-\pi },$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{-\pi }$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(1,2),(1,-2),(-1,-1).$

So, the correct answer is "I, II and III."
